overview.title: How the Chart Suggestion tool works

blocks.content: The Chart Suggestion tool reads the analytical roles of your selected columns and proposes suitable chart types, ranked by fit. The logic is inspired by Tableau's "Show Me" and the Minitab Graph Builder.
The quickest entry point is the "Suggest Chart" button in the Worksheet toolbar. Select one or more columns first.
Pick one or more columns in the Worksheet. From the combination of their {{term:skalenniveau|roles}} (Continuous, Categorical, Ordinal, Date) we derive the most fitting visualization type.
On the left you see the ranked suggestions in ranked order, the best fit on top. On the right we render a preview of the selected chart type. Click a suggestion to switch the preview.
Some charts only make sense above a minimum n. With n < 20, the histogram is hidden in favor of boxplot and individual-value-plot. A control chart needs at least 25 data points.

Most previews carry an "Open in module" button above the chart. It spawns a new instance of the full module (histogram, boxplot, individual-value plot, run chart, bar chart, Pareto chart, mosaic plot, heatmap, probability plot, or XY plot) in the same phase area, with the selected columns already wired up — so you can carry on with annotations, reference lines, axis tuning, or export. For pie, the scatter matrix and the preview-only combinations (main effects, interaction, marginal distributions, CUSUM) there is no target module — the button is hidden there.

Selecting three or more continuous columns suggests a scatter matrix (SPLOM). The preview renders an n×n grid of small scatter plots for all column pairs; the diagonal shows the column name. With more than six columns only the first six are displayed — a performance and readability limit.

For the combination "date + continuous" the suggestion includes a {{term:regelkarte|control chart}}. The preview automatically computes an I-chart (Individuals) with the {{term:mittellinie|centerline}} at the mean, ±3σ limits (σ derived from the mean moving range, d2=1.128) and observations sorted by date. Switch to the full Control-chart module under "Control" for X̄/R, X̄/S, or Phase-I exclusions.
